text:
## Abstract

This study investigates whether expression studies involving Escherichia coli and the antibiotic ciprofloxacin exist in GEO. Using the GEO database with the query "Escherichia coli" and the term "ciprofloxacin," we identified 37 Series-type expression studies, with metadata for the top 10 returned. These studies encompass transcriptomic responses to ciprofloxacin exposure, mechanisms of resistance, metabolic adaptation, and other antibiotic-related contexts. The availability of these datasets is crucial for researchers interested in bacterial antibiotic stress responses, resistance mechanisms, and systems-level transcriptomic adaptation.

## I. Introduction

### Background
Escherichia coli is a model organism used extensively in microbiology and antibiotic resistance research. Ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, is widely used against E. coli infections, and understanding the transcriptomic responses can reveal mechanisms of resistance, tolerance, and cellular adaptation.

### Literature Review
No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO metadata highlighted studies by their titles, summaries, and PubMed linkages where available.

### Knowledge Gap
Prior to this query, it was unclear how many expression studies in E. coli addressed ciprofloxacin exposure, what experimental contexts were represented, and the accessibility of raw and processed expression values.

### Objective & Hypothesis
The objective was to identify and catalog E. coli expression studies involving ciprofloxacin available in GEO. The hypothesis was that such studies exist and address antibiotic response and resistance phenomena.

## II. Materials and Methods

### Study Design
The study used GEO’s Series database for processed expression studies in E. coli subjected to ciprofloxacin. The search was filtered for Series-type entries (the standard analytic unit in GEO).

### Materials
- Database: NCBI GEO, accessed via functions.geo_search

### Procedures
1. Query GEO with:
   - organism: "Escherichia coli"
   - term: "ciprofloxacin"
   - entry_type: "gse" (Series)
   - max_results: 10
2. Capture: total count; metadata for the top 10 Series; FTP download links for raw/processed data.

### Statistical Analysis
- Count of studies derived from GEO’s ‘total_count’ field.
- Titles and summaries reviewed; PubMed IDs checked for linkage.
- Proportion of studies returned (10/37; API capped at 10).

## III. Results

### Data Presentation

**Table 1. E. coli GEO Expression Studies Involving Ciprofloxacin (Top 10 Metadata Snapshot)**

| GEO Accession | Title | Sample Count | Platform | Date Public | PubMed ID | FTP Directory | Ciprofloxacin Context |
|---------------|-------|--------------|----------|-------------|-----------|---------------|----------------------|
| GSE309890     | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence... | 6 | GPL24659 | 2026-02-01 | - | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/) | Mutational bias includes ciprofloxacin |
| GSE276254     | A dual-mechanism antimicrobial peptide...               | 51 | GPL21222 | 2025-08-25 | 40879398 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE276nnn/GSE276254/) | Resistance to ciprofloxacin reduced |
| GSE283264     | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RNA-Seq) | 25 | GPL32081 | 2025-06-24 | 40804527 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/) | Ciprofloxacin included by text match |
| GSE295494     | Revealing Transcriptomic Responses during Early Antibiotic Exposure | 42 | GPL26592 | 2025-05-01 | 41805196 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/) | Time-resolved cipro exposure |
| GSE292923     | RNA-seq effect of purA on transcriptome during cipro treatment | 4 | GPL18133 | 2025-03-25 | 42079445 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/) | Transcriptome before/after cipro |
| GSE275261     | Differential effects of IMPDH inhibition...            | 24 | GPL22143 | 2024-08-25 | 39235234 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/) | E. coli + cipro 1h exposure |
| GSE272161     | Elementary 3D organization of E. coli genome           | 64 | GPL32081 | 2025-06-24 | 40804527 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/) | Text match in methods |
| GSE272160     | Elementary 3D organization (RedC)                      | 4 | GPL32081 | 2025-06-24 | 40804527 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/) | Text match, unclear importance |
| GSE272159     | Elementary 3D organization (MicroC)                    | 33 | GPL32081 | 2025-06-24 | 40804527 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/) | Contains cipro samples |
| GSE272158     | Elementary 3D organization (HiC)                       | 2 | GPL32081 | 2025-06-24 | 40804527 | [FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/) | Text match, unclear importance |

### Findings
- 37 Series-type GEO studies were identified as relevant by the search.
- Metadata for the top 10 is presented above, covering sample counts, platforms, and FTP links.
- Most studies focus on transcriptomic effects during or after ciprofloxacin exposure.
- Some studies include ciprofloxacin as one of several antibiotics.

## IV. Discussion

### Interpretation
The GEO database contains 37 expression profiling studies for E. coli involving ciprofloxacin, spanning diverse experimental contexts from resistance emergence to metabolic responses and systems biology.

### Context
Returned metadata indicates studies on mutational resistance, mechanisms of tolerance, early antibiotic adaptation, and gene expression shifts. FTP links provide access to actual data files.

### Limitations
Only metadata for the top 10 studies is shown here, due to the API’s response cap. Expression values themselves are not included and must be downloaded directly via provided FTP links. Some studies may include ciprofloxacin as a minor component or only in supplemental experiments.

### Conclusion & Future Directions
E. coli expression studies involving ciprofloxacin are well represented in GEO. Download studies matching your interest from the FTP links for detailed transcriptomic analyses. Future queries could narrow by tissue, mutant strain, or antibiotic dosage, or retrieve all 37 study accessions.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO Series Search, “Escherichia coli” AND “ciprofloxacin”, https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gds&term=%22Escherichia%20coli%22%5BOrganism%5D%20AND%20%28ciprofloxacin%29%20AND%20%22gse%22%5BFilter%5D&retmax=10

## Acknowledgments

The National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GEO data repository.
